items.title: Richard Wyands interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002
items.q: I did this date with Etta Jones, “Don’t Go to Strangers.” ... in the case of Etta Jones, she knew the tunes, she knew the keys, I think she did, and we would get it together and decide on the changes, quickly, very quickly.

ctx.x: Do you recall the first recording date in New York that you made?

In New York. I think it was with Jerome Richardson. It was called “Roamin’ with Richardson” for Prestige. And that particular date I think the coordinator, somebody by the name of — oh I can’t think of his name — he got me on a lot of other dates for Prestige. That one date I did with Jerome did it, really. I got more calls from Prestige to do more dates. And as a result I did this date with Etta Jones, “Don’t Go to Strangers.” And that luckily, fortunately, turned out pretty good.
It’s curious when a record like that takes off. I’m wondering when you recorded it, did it make a particular impression on you?
